prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: In frames 1 and 2, the depth map shows the camera wearer's own fingers/hand within centimetres (0.05–0.1 m) occluding almost the entire field of view, before revealing an indoor room layout in frames 3 to 5 with a very bright vertical partition wall/booth on the right within arm's reach (about 0.5–0.8 m away) and a darker open corridor/room to the left. On the left in frame 3, a standing woman is silhouetted at roughly 1.2–1.5 m distance, positioned about 0.5–1.0 m in front of a lower white chair and small side table behind and below her, while an adjacent room behind a glass partition lies further back (3–5+ m). From frame 3 to frame 5, as the camera wearer turns rightward and moves slightly past the booth, the woman shifts toward the lower-left edge, becoming progressively cropped out of view and appearing darker/further relative to the bright right-hand partition. The woman's right profile contour clearly shows she faces right and slightly downward toward the handheld object within her arm's reach, looking away from the camera wearer. Compared to RGB, the depth map more clearly separates the foreground woman from the chair and table behind her and highlights the immediate proximity of the right-hand booth wall, though it is unreliable on the blurred close-up skin in frame 1 (assigning inconsistent mid-grey depth to the upper-left portion) and makes the glass-enclosed room in the background completely black without detailed room geometry.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map captures the severe near-field occlusion in frames 1 and 2 as large 'person' masks covering the camera wearer's own close-up hand (at <0.1 m), and then in frames 3 to 5 segments the woman on the left (1.2–1.5 m away), the cell phone in her hands (about 0.3 m in front of her chest), the chair behind and below her (at ~1.8–2.2 m), and the tall booth/enclosure on the right (at ~0.5–0.8 m, mislabelled as 'refrigerator'). In frame 3, the woman's silhouette faces right in profile, looking down toward the cell phone held within her arm's reach rather than toward the camera wearer, while the chair sits just behind her lower torso and the right-hand booth is within the camera wearer's arm's reach. Across frames 3 to 5, as the camera turns right, the woman and chair shift leftward and downward until only her lower arms, head edge, and a small sliver of the chair remain visible at the bottom-left of frame 5, while the right-hand enclosure expands to fill the right half of the frame. The map helps isolate the tiny cell phone mask in frame 3 and the partially occluded chair edge in frame 5 against dark clothing and clutter in the RGB image. However, it is unreliable where it misclassifies a gap between fingers in frame 2 as a 'fork', labels the glass-and-wall booth in frames 3 and 5 as a 'refrigerator' while missing it entirely in frame 4, and fails to segment the phone in frames 4 and 5 or the small table and background furniture.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely blank in frames 1, 2, 4, and 5, detecting a yellow body skeleton only in frame 3 for the woman standing on the left at roughly 1.2–1.5 m from the camera wearer. In frame 3, the plotted head keypoints (eyes, nose, and ear above the shoulder) and the V-shaped right upper-arm and forearm linkage show her facing right in profile with her head tilted slightly down and her right arm bent upward, holding her hands within arm's reach in front of her chest and looking away from the camera wearer. The skeleton places her upper torso in the left-centre foreground above the level of the nearby chair, while no other people are present in the scene. Across the 5-frame sequence, pose tracking fails during the extreme close-up hand occlusion in frames 1–2 and drops out again in frames 4–5 as the camera turns right and the woman's body becomes increasingly cropped at the lower-left border. While the frame 3 skeleton makes the exact elbow flexion and shoulder-to-wrist geometry through her dark sleeve easier to see than in the RGB alone, the map is largely unreliable because it misses all magenta hand/finger keypoints (both the camera wearer's close-up hand in frames 1–2 and the woman's hands on her phone in frames 3–5), collapses her left and right arm joints together, and fails to track her partial profile in frames 4 and 5.
